Start with the actual agreement

  1. Collect the invoice, out-gate and return receipts, plus the tariff, service contract or provider addendum effective for this move.
  2. Enter one container and its allocated detention amount. Separate chassis charges, demurrage, taxes and unrelated fees.
  3. Use a documented last free day, or calculate one with the agreement’s counting rules. Enter the exact daily rates.
  4. Verify dates, attach supporting records to your own email, and review the draft before sending it through the provider’s process.
No outdated carrier presets. A rate printed on an invoice is a claim to check, not independent proof of the correct rate.

Billing clocks are separate checks

FMC: for covered US maritime invoices, ocean carriers / terminals use the last incurred charge; NVOCCs use the issue date of the underlying invoice. The issuance window is 30 calendar days. Scope excludes billing among ocean carriers and terminals.

UIIA: E.6.c uses return + 60 days, with a conditional wrong-party correction window capped at 90 days. That contractual check does not override an applicable FMC requirement.

Reply promptly: FMC’s minimum request window runs from issuance; the UIIA default process runs from receipt. Provider terms and extensions also matter. The app shows each clock separately.

The former FMC §541.4 recipient restriction was set aside. This app does not apply it.

How the math works

Day 1 of a rate step is counted after the last free day. Choose whether tier progression uses chargeable days or elapsed calendar days. Convert any tariff that numbers days from pickup before entering its tiers.

Working days skip only your selected weekdays and entered holiday dates. Federal dates are a reference list, never automatically applied. Calendar-day free time ignores those exclusions.

Disputed operational days stay in the baseline calculation. Their amount is shown separately without moving later rate steps. A closure or refused return is evidence to review, not an automatic waiver.

Pickup can be charged when free time is zero and counting starts on pickup. Return is included only if selected. Values use whole cents and terminal-local calendar dates.

What this tool does—and what needs a person

It calculates your entered rules, flags date and invoice-content issues, organizes evidence references, and prepares review drafts.

It cannot verify agreements, read PDFs, contact terminals, send disputes, or determine the final amount legally payable. It does not handle combined demurrage/detention tariffs, partial daily rates, multiple currencies or multiple containers in one calculation.

Files are not attached here. Record their filenames in the evidence section and retain the originals. “Verified” means you checked the source, not that this app authenticated it.

No analytics or tracking. Without an account, nothing leaves this browser and saved cases stay here. If you sign in, Google’s Firebase sign-in loads and your saved cases are also kept in your account. Downloads contain the details you choose to export.

Build a useful record of results

Keep a case for each reviewed container. Save the version you send, note the submission date, and record the provider’s response.

Enter a confirmed credit only after a written credit or refund is received. The register totals actual credits separately from calculated differences.

Use the printable report for an internal review or supporting attachment. Export case backups to move your work between devices. Imports preserve case identity and skip cases already present; they never overwrite existing work.

Import from a spreadsheet

Paste cells from Excel or Google Sheets, or upload CSV, TSV or text.

For .xlsx files, export the Entry sheet as CSV or copy its cells below. No Google account connection is needed.

Two supported formats

One invoice: use the Excel template. Fill the Value column, then copy the Field and Value columns, including the header.

Several invoices: use a table with field names across the first row and one container per row.

  1. Use YYYY-MM-DD dates.
  2. Enter a documented last free day, or explicitly enter the number of free days.
  3. Enter rates as 1-3:100; 4-6:150; 7+:200.
  4. Review the preview. Invalid rows block the import. Duplicate company/invoice/container records are skipped.

Source and gate verification reset on spreadsheet import. Backups retain their original review state.

Formatting reference

Use the field names below or their displayed labels. Optional fields can be omitted. The preview shows the resulting values. Blank free days never mean zero.

Tutorial

A captioned walkthrough of version 3 using fictional data. Pause whenever you need to.

1. Start with the records

Collect the invoice, gate-out and return receipts, and the agreement effective for that move. Review one container and its allocated detention charge at a time.

2. Enter or import the information

Use Invoice review for manual entry. For spreadsheets, fill the template, copy the Field and Value columns including the header, and paste into Import. Preview the values before importing. The preview is a format check, not verification of the underlying documents.

3. Check free time and rates

The numeric free-days field controls the calculation. Source notes describe the supporting document. Enter a last free day directly if you have one. Otherwise set the number of free days, working/calendar basis and start day. Confirm how rate steps progress.

4. Read the separate results

The baseline is the calculation under your entries. Billed minus baseline is a difference to investigate. Billing deadlines and invoice-content checks are separate. An operational date selected for review stays in the baseline and is not automatically waived.

5. Save and prepare your response

Keep evidence references, edit the draft, and print a review report if useful. Submit through the provider’s own process. Enter the submission date afterward. Record credits only when documented.

6. Keep a backup

Save case keeps work in the current browser. Export backup downloads a portable copy. Use Saved cases to restore a backup. Export before switching devices, changing the app file location or clearing browser data.

The tutorial uses a test case with a $650 baseline and a $100 difference. These are fictional values, not current carrier rates or promised savings.

Review support, not a payment verdict. Your applicable agreement, shipment facts and governing rules control. Timing flags and calculated differences are not guaranteed recoveries.
